body:
I kept testing and one of the root causes seems to be that `System.Native` does not load properly.
This is apparent when calling, for example, `GD.Print("Random number: " + new System.Random().Next()))` - the following output will get logged to the browser console:
```
Attempting to load: 'System.Native'.
DllImport error loading library '.mono/assemblies/Debug/System.Native': ''.
DllImport error loading library '.mono/assemblies/Debug/System.Native.wasm': ''.
DllImport error loading library './lib/System.Native': ''.
DllImport error loading library './lib/System.Native.wasm': ''.
DllImport loaded library 'System.Native'.
DllImport searching in: 'System.Native' ('System.Native').
Searching for 'SystemNative_GetNonCryptographicallySecureRandomBytes'.
Probing 'SystemNative_GetNonCryptographicallySecureRandomBytes'.
Found as 'SystemNative_GetNonCryptographicallySecureRandomBytes'.
DllImport searching in: 'System.Native' ('System.Native').
Searching for 'SystemNative_LChflagsCanSetHiddenFlag'.
Probing 'SystemNative_LChflagsCanSetHiddenFlag'.
Found as 'SystemNative_LChflagsCanSetHiddenFlag'.
```
Surprisingly, a random number *is* correctly printed, but the logs suggest that `System.Native` wasn't completely/correctly loaded.

According to @andy-noisyduck on issue [#38810](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/38810), `System.Random` is used by `ThreadPool.QueueSegment` internally, so you can end up running into this when using Tasks.

EDIT: I'm now suspecting this is an unrelated bug, because using `System.Random` alone does *not* break the godot-mono glue, but `System.Threading.Tasks` does.
